On the one hand, Because the gangs, some of the gangs are listed in the Secretary-General report on children in armed conflict as utilizing children, recruiting children. Clearly, when operations will take place and there will be more, I would say, results of those operations, hopefully capturing gang leaders, gang members, there'll be also, let's say, recovering of children. And minors under 18, as you know, according to UN instruments, are victims first and foremost. So they need to be channeled through the social services passing through some mechanisms that we have through our agencies. UNICEF have particular transition centers for children to have short stays there so they can get psychosocial support and other means. But in the long run— in the long run, and we are working with the Haitians and the institutions on that, we are establishing a DDR program because then you need to link those children released or recovered of the gangs to those transition centers, but then to vocational trainings, to different capacity-building activities so they can be linked afterwards to job opportunities. And I'm saying this because in all these steps, we need to avoid or to reduce the risks of the children getting back to the gangs. And also, we need to implement, again, preventive measures, because while we are hoping and confident that we can recover minors, that some minors will be released, we don't want the gangs at the same time to continue recruiting children and children be prone or subject to those activities. So we need to— part of the program should be violence reduction, community violence reduction activities that include investment and possibilities of getting opportunities currently already for the children that we can consider, or this UN system can consider children at risk. So they can— so it's, I would say, an overall general two-pronged approach in that sense. A preventive one, but also once established or implemented to those that will be recovered either in the operations by the JSF or that the other groups are— will be more willing to start releasing them. So the Prime Minister— the Council of Ministers led by the Prime Minister, is in charge and in accordance with an instrument that they signed among the different political forces, he will stay in power until elections happen and there will be a more, let's say, going back to democratic order. Evidently, as I mentioned, there's a link between security conditions, particularly in the capital and in other departments, because those departments and the capital have around 54-55% of the overall electorate registered these days. So security needs to improve in those areas. So Candidates can campaign, and eventually on election day, people can vote in a free manner. So for now, we have a transitional government, again, just recapitulating, led by the Prime Minister, and will stay until elections happen, but we hope it will happen soon. That's the aim. That's part of their priorities of the current government: elections, security, and humanitarian situation.
